cards.ex: Necesitamos completar la inscripción de su hijo.
cards.exEn: We need to complete your child's enrollment.
cards.region: "Matrícula" is also common, especially in Central and South America.

cards.ex: Por favor, llene el formulario de registro.
cards.exEn: Please fill out the registration form.
cards.region: "Llenar" is Latin American; "rellenar" is Spain.

cards.ex: Necesito ver el acta de nacimiento de su hija.
cards.exEn: I need to see your daughter's birth certificate.
cards.region: "Acta" is Mexican. Elsewhere: "certificado de nacimiento" or "partida de nacimiento". "Acta" is feminine but takes "el".
cards.flag: Confirm which term Central American families use most.

cards.ex: Necesitamos un comprobante de domicilio, como un recibo de luz.
cards.exEn: We need proof of address, such as a utility bill.
cards.region: "Comprobante de residencia" is also used.

cards.ex: Traiga la cartilla de vacunación de su hijo.
cards.exEn: Please bring your child's immunization record.
cards.region: "Cartilla" is Mexican. Elsewhere: "registro de vacunas" or "carné de vacunas".
cards.flag: Which term do US school forms use in Spanish? Possibly "registro de vacunas".

cards.es: el padre, la madre o el tutor legal
cards.pron: el PAH-dreh, lah MAH-dreh oh el too-TOR leh-GAHL
cards.ex: El padre, la madre o el tutor legal debe firmar aquí.
cards.exEn: The parent or legal guardian must sign here.
cards.region: "Tutor" (m.) / "tutora" (f.). Understood everywhere.

cards.ex: Necesito un número de contacto de emergencia.
cards.exEn: I need an emergency contact number.

cards.es: la encuesta del idioma del hogar
cards.pron: lah en-KWES-tah del ee-DYOH-mah del oh-GAR
cards.ex: Por favor, conteste la encuesta del idioma del hogar.
cards.exEn: Please answer the home language survey.
cards.flag: Official title varies by district. Use the district's own Spanish form title.

cards.ex: ¿En qué grado estaba su hijo en su escuela anterior?
cards.exEn: What grade was your child in at the previous school?
cards.region: "Grado" in Mexico, Central America, US. South America often says "curso" or "año".

cards.ex: ¿Cuál es el nombre de la escuela anterior?
cards.exEn: What is the name of the previous school?
cards.region: "Colegio" can mean a private school in some countries. "Escuela" is safest.

cards.ex: Vamos a solicitar el expediente escolar de su hijo.
cards.exEn: We are going to request your child's school records.
cards.region: "Historial académico" is also used for transcripts.
cards.flag: "Expediente" vs. "récord" (US Spanish). Confirm what parents expect.

cards.ex: Necesito una identificación con foto.
cards.exEn: I need a photo ID.
cards.region: "Credencial" (Mexico), "cédula" (many Central/South American countries), "DNI" (Peru, Argentina).

cards.es: almuerzo gratuito o a precio reducido
cards.pron: ahl-MWER-soh grah-TWEE-toh oh ah PREH-syoh reh-doo-SEE-doh
cards.ex: Su hijo puede calificar para el almuerzo gratuito o a precio reducido.
cards.exEn: Your child may qualify for free or reduced-price lunch.
cards.region: In Mexico "almuerzo" can mean a late-morning meal and "comida" the midday meal. In US schools "almuerzo" is widely understood.
cards.flag: Is "almuerzo" or "comida" clearer for Mexican families?

cards.ex: El autobús escolar pasa a las siete de la mañana.
cards.exEn: The school bus comes at seven in the morning.
cards.region: "Camión" (Mexico), "bus" (Central America), "guagua" (Caribbean). "Autobús" works everywhere.

cards.ex: La asistencia de su hijo es muy importante.
cards.exEn: Your child's attendance is very important.

cards.ex: Su hijo tiene tres ausencias esta semana.
cards.exEn: Your child has three absences this week.
cards.region: "Falta" is very common in Mexico ("faltó" = was absent). "Inasistencia" is used in Colombia and others.

cards.ex: Su hija tiene varias tardanzas este mes.
cards.exEn: Your daughter has several tardies this month.
cards.region: "Retardo" is Mexican school usage. "Tardanza" is common in Central America and the Caribbean.
cards.flag: Confirm "retardo" vs. "tardanza" for your families.

cards.ex: Con una nota del médico, la ausencia es justificada.
cards.exEn: With a doctor's note, the absence is excused.

cards.ex: Esta ausencia es injustificada.
cards.exEn: This absence is unexcused.

cards.ex: El ausentismo escolar puede tener consecuencias legales.
cards.exEn: Truancy can have legal consequences.
cards.region: Spain writes "absentismo". Latin America uses "ausentismo".
cards.flag: Is there a gentler, more common phrase parents would recognize?

cards.ex: Por favor, traiga una nota del médico.
cards.exEn: Please bring a doctor's note.
cards.region: "Justificante médico" (Mexico), "excusa médica" (Puerto Rico), "certificado médico" (South America).
cards.flag: Regional assignments of these alternatives.

cards.ex: Por favor, venga a recoger a su hijo.
cards.exEn: Please come pick up your child.
cards.region: "Recoger" is fine everywhere. Avoid "coger", which is vulgar in Mexico and Argentina.

cards.ex: Puede dejar a su hijo a las ocho de la mañana.
cards.exEn: You can drop off your child at eight in the morning.
cards.region: "Dejar" or "llevar" (to take). Both are natural.

cards.ex: El viernes hay salida anticipada a la una.
cards.exEn: On Friday there is early dismissal at one o'clock.
cards.region: Many US families say "salida temprano", which is not standard grammar.
cards.flag: "Salida anticipada" vs. "salida temprana". Please check.

cards.ex: ¿Su hijo estuvo enfermo ayer?
cards.exEn: Was your child sick yesterday?
cards.region: "Estar enfermo" = sick now. "Ser enfermo" would mean chronically ill.

cards.ex: Por favor, llame a la escuela si su hijo va a faltar.
cards.exEn: Please call the school if your child is going to be absent.

cards.ex: Su hijo faltó a clases el lunes.
cards.exEn: Your child missed class on Monday.
cards.region: "Faltar" is the usual verb for being absent in Mexico and Central America.

cards.ex: Enviaremos la boleta de calificaciones a su casa.
cards.exEn: We will send the report card home.
cards.region: "Boleta" (Mexico, Central America, Peru). "Libreta" (Dominican Republic, Venezuela, others). "Tarjeta de calificaciones" (Puerto Rico). "Informe de notas" (parts of South America).
cards.flag: Regional assignments of boleta / libreta / tarjeta.

cards.ex: La calificación de su hijo en matemáticas es una B.
cards.exEn: Your child's math grade is a B.
cards.region: "Nota" is common in Central and South America and Spain. "Calificación" is Mexican.

cards.ex: Su hija va a aprobar el año escolar.
cards.exEn: Your daughter is going to pass the school year.

cards.ex: Su hijo está en riesgo de reprobar la materia.
cards.exEn: Your child is at risk of failing the subject.
cards.region: "Reprobar" (Mexico, Central America). "Perder la materia" (Colombia, Venezuela). Avoid "suspender": in Spain it means to fail, in Latin America it means to suspend.
cards.flag: Confirm "reprobar" is understood in Caribbean and South American communities.

cards.ex: Recibirá un informe de progreso cada seis semanas.
cards.exEn: You will receive a progress report every six weeks.

cards.es: la reunión de padres y maestros
cards.pron: lah reh-oo-NYOHN deh PAH-dres ee mah-ES-tros
cards.ex: La reunión de padres y maestros es el jueves.
cards.exEn: The parent-teacher conference is on Thursday.
cards.region: "Maestro" (Mexico, Central America). "Profesor" is common in secondary school and South America.

cards.ex: Su hijo no entregó la tarea.
cards.exEn: Your child did not turn in the homework.
cards.region: "Deberes" is Spain. Use "tarea" in Latin America.

cards.ex: El examen es el próximo martes.
cards.exEn: The exam is next Tuesday.
cards.region: "Prueba" is also common (Central and South America).

cards.ex: Su hijo tomará la prueba estandarizada en abril.
cards.exEn: Your child will take the standardized test in April.
cards.flag: "Prueba" vs. "examen" estandarizado. Which is more natural?

cards.ex: ¿En qué materia necesita ayuda?
cards.exEn: In which subject does he need help?
cards.region: "Asignatura" is more formal. "Clase" is also used informally.

cards.ex: Le recomendamos que repita el grado.
cards.exEn: We recommend that he repeat the grade.
cards.region: Sensitive topic. Say it slowly and clearly.
cards.flag: Is there a softer phrase, such as "permanecer en el mismo grado"?

cards.ex: Su hija puede recibir tutorías después de la escuela.
cards.exEn: Your daughter can receive tutoring after school.
cards.region: "Clases de apoyo" or "clases de refuerzo" are also used.
cards.flag: Which is more familiar to families: "tutorías" or "clases de refuerzo"?

cards.ex: El promedio de su hijo es 3.2.
cards.exEn: Your child's GPA is 3.2.
cards.region: "Promedio" alone is common.
cards.flag: Parents may not know the US GPA system. Add a short explanation.

cards.ex: El comportamiento de su hijo ha mejorado.
cards.exEn: Your child's behavior has improved.
cards.region: "Conducta" is common on report cards.

cards.ex: Su hijo tendrá detención después de clases.
cards.exEn: Your child will have detention after school.
cards.flag: "Detención" can sound like arrest. Maybe "castigo" or "tiempo de corrección"? Please verify.

cards.ex: La suspensión es por dos días.
cards.exEn: The suspension is for two days.
cards.region: In Spain "suspender" can mean to fail. Context makes it clear.

cards.ex: La escuela está considerando la expulsión.
cards.exEn: The school is considering expulsion.

cards.ex: Su hijo recibió un reporte disciplinario.
cards.exEn: Your child received a disciplinary report.
cards.region: "Informe" is the Spain-style word. "Reporte" is common in Mexico and the US.
cards.flag: "Reporte" vs. "informe disciplinario".

cards.ex: Tomamos muy en serio el acoso escolar.
cards.exEn: We take bullying very seriously.
cards.region: "Bullying" is widely used in Mexico. "Matoneo" (Colombia), "hostigamiento" (Peru).

cards.ex: Su hijo participó en una pelea.
cards.exEn: Your child took part in a fight.
cards.region: "Pleito" is also used in Mexico. "Pelea" is understood everywhere.

cards.ex: Su hijo le pegó a otro estudiante.
cards.exEn: Your child hit another student.

cards.ex: Por favor, revise las reglas de la escuela con su hijo.
cards.exEn: Please review the school rules with your child.
cards.region: "Reglamento escolar" is the formal rulebook.

cards.ex: Cada falta tiene una consecuencia.
cards.exEn: Every violation has a consequence.

cards.ex: Esta es una advertencia por escrito.
cards.exEn: This is a written warning.

cards.ex: La directora quiere hablar con usted.
cards.exEn: The principal wants to speak with you.
cards.region: Assistant principal: "subdirector" / "subdirectora".

cards.es: el consejero escolar / la consejera escolar
cards.ex: La consejera escolar puede ayudar a su hijo.
cards.exEn: The school counselor can help your child.
cards.region: "Orientador" is used in some countries.
cards.flag: Is "consejero" widely understood, or would "orientador" be better for some families?

cards.ex: No se permite el celular durante la clase.
cards.exEn: Cell phones are not allowed during class.
cards.region: "Celular" (Latin America). "Móvil" (Spain).

cards.ex: Su hijo podría recibir servicios de educación especial.
cards.exEn: Your child could receive special education services.

cards.ex: Vamos a revisar el IEP de su hijo.
cards.exEn: We are going to review your child's IEP.
cards.region: Many families just say "IEP" using the English letters.
cards.flag: Official Spanish title varies ("Individualizado" vs. "Individualizada"). Use the district's wording.

cards.ex: Su hijo necesita una evaluación.
cards.exEn: Your child needs an evaluation.

cards.ex: Necesitamos su consentimiento por escrito.
cards.exEn: We need your written consent.

cards.ex: Una discapacidad no define a su hijo.
cards.exEn: A disability does not define your child.
cards.region: Do not use "incapacidad". In Mexico it means medical leave or inability.

cards.ex: La evaluación indica una discapacidad de aprendizaje.
cards.exEn: The evaluation indicates a learning disability.
cards.region: "Dificultad de aprendizaje" and "trastorno del aprendizaje" are also used.
cards.flag: Which phrase is least stigmatizing and most familiar to parents?

cards.ex: Su hijo recibirá adaptaciones en los exámenes.
cards.exEn: Your child will receive accommodations on tests.
cards.region: "Acomodaciones" is an English-influenced form used in some US materials.
cards.flag: "Adaptaciones" vs. "acomodaciones". Check what districts use.

cards.ex: Estos servicios son gratuitos.
cards.exEn: These services are free.

cards.ex: Su hija recibirá terapia del habla dos veces por semana.
cards.exEn: Your daughter will receive speech therapy twice a week.
cards.region: "Terapia de lenguaje" is also common, especially in Mexico.
cards.flag: "Habla" vs. "lenguaje". Confirm.

cards.ex: La terapia ocupacional ayuda con la escritura.
cards.exEn: Occupational therapy helps with handwriting.

cards.ex: Le voy a explicar los derechos de los padres.
cards.exEn: I am going to explain the parent rights to you.
cards.region: Often printed as "Aviso de garantías procesales"; ask which wording the district uses.
cards.flag: "Aviso de garantías procesales" (procedural safeguards). Please verify.

cards.ex: Hay un intérprete disponible sin costo.
cards.exEn: An interpreter is available at no cost.
cards.region: "Traductor" is a written translator. An interpreter speaks. Many parents say "traductor" for both.

cards.ex: Su hijo es un estudiante que aprende inglés.
cards.exEn: Your child is an English learner.
cards.flag: Districts may use "aprendiz de inglés" or "estudiante de inglés como segundo idioma". Please verify the usual term.

cards.es: la enfermera escolar / el enfermero escolar
cards.ex: La enfermera escolar revisó a su hijo.
cards.exEn: The school nurse checked your child.

cards.ex: Su hijo tiene fiebre. Por favor, venga a recogerlo.
cards.exEn: Your child has a fever. Please come pick him up.
cards.region: "Calentura" means fever in some regions but sounds odd or crude elsewhere. Use "fiebre".

cards.ex: Su hija necesita una vacuna antes de entrar a la escuela.
cards.exEn: Your daughter needs a vaccine before starting school.

cards.ex: ¿Su hijo tiene alguna alergia?
cards.exEn: Does your child have any allergies?

cards.ex: Necesitamos una autorización para darle el medicamento.
cards.exEn: We need authorization to give him the medication.
cards.region: "Medicina" is the everyday word.

cards.ex: Su hijo vomitó en la clase.
cards.exEn: Your child vomited in class.
cards.region: "Devolver" or "regresar" are informal in some regions. "Vomitar" is clear everywhere.

cards.ex: Su hija tiene dolor de estómago.
cards.exEn: Your daughter has a stomachache.
cards.region: "Dolor de panza" is informal in Mexico and Central America, especially with children.

cards.ex: Su hijo se queja de dolor de cabeza.
cards.exEn: Your child is complaining of a headache.

cards.ex: Encontramos piojos en el cabello de su hija.
cards.exEn: We found lice in your daughter's hair.

cards.ex: Es una enfermedad contagiosa.
cards.exEn: It is a contagious illness.

cards.ex: Su hijo debe traer su inhalador para el asma.
cards.exEn: Your child should bring his asthma inhaler.
cards.region: "La bomba" is used for an inhaler among some Puerto Rican and Dominican families.
cards.flag: "Bomba" for inhaler: confirm regions. "Asma" takes the article "el" (el asma) though it is feminine.

cards.ex: Su hijo tuvo una lesión en el recreo.
cards.exEn: Your child had an injury at recess.
cards.region: "Herida" is an open wound. "Lesión" is the general term. "Golpe" = bump or blow.

cards.ex: Hoy tuvimos un simulacro de incendio.
cards.exEn: Today we had a fire drill.
cards.region: "Simulacro" is widely used (earthquake drills in Mexico).

cards.ex: La escuela estuvo en cierre de emergencia por precaución.
cards.exEn: The school was in lockdown as a precaution.
cards.flag: No standard term. Maybe "encierro de seguridad" or "confinamiento". Please verify.
